## Verdict

The recorded refutation-target fails. Bind the successor lean on the open fork that retargets enforcement to existing merge-gate / branch-gate checks plus `verify:docs-impact`. Tiers 1-3 as filed cannot bind as merge authority or as a sufficient replacement for advisory pre-PR.

Re-measured at dispatch SHA `7712f482781c4885fd9d395756e2c316785730dd`: `git grep` of `pr:ready` / `pre-pr-complete` / `pre-pr-gate` is empty; `.github/workflows/` is branch-gate, ci, ci-lane, docs-site, greenfield-python-free-smoke, npm-publish, one-pr-unit-merge-group, release; `content/skills/deft-directive-pre-pr/SKILL.md` still names the RWLDL loop and the merge-chokepoint `deft check`, including "Do not add a fourth probe (#2893 / #4379)".

## F1 — Gitignored marker cannot prove the skill ran

`blocks-the-design`

**Evidence:** AC3 requires CI to fail when `.deft/pre-pr-complete.<head-sha>.json` is absent for the PR head. AC7 gitignores those files and then has the Action read a workflow-scoped artifact or a git-tracked hash-only manifest. At this SHA `.gitignore` already ignores `.deft/*` except `approved-scope/` and `intent-constraint/`. A `pull_request` checkout does not contain the author's gitignored working tree. GitHub Actions artifacts come from workflow runs, not from a local `task pr:ready`. A committed hash-only JSON is an agent-authored attestation of `git rev-parse HEAD`.

**Failure mode:** Implementers commit a forgeable SHA JSON, or CI re-runs `task check` / `git diff`, which `check:merge` already runs inside Merge gate. Swarm worktrees keep `.deft/` as local scratch, so the marker never reaches CI.

**Disposition:** Drop Tiers 2-3 as merge-gate proof. A local convenience alias, if any, must not mint a required artifact.

## F2 — Whole-body `- [ ]` fail-closed hits Post-Merge

`blocks-the-design`

**Evidence:** `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` at this SHA has `## Checklist` (three `- [ ]` boxes) and `## Post-Merge` (two more: verify issue auto-close after squash merge; enable branch protection on `master`). Tier 1 fails if any `- [ ]` lacks an `N/A -- <reason>` suffix. AC1 treats an empty or unchecked template checklist as merge-blocking.

**Failure mode:** A template-compliant PR is red at open until agents tick post-merge boxes early or stamp `N/A --` on work defined to happen after merge. Leftover-complete PRs that compose only the Documentation impact block (#4293) omit those boxes and fail the same parser.

**Disposition:** Tier 1 as specified cannot bind. Checkbox CI is the wrong instrument.

## F3 — `pre-pr-gate / checklist` is the wrong authority name

`blocks-the-design`

**Evidence:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` job/check map (#3168) makes aggregators the branch-protection SoT; the only YES row is `TypeScript (build + lint + test)`; `Merge gate (task check)` is `no` and skips when `artifact_only`. `verify:docs-impact` is already a Merge-gate step (`task verify:docs-impact -- --pr`, primary and failover). `branch-gate.yml` is the existing `opened/synchronize/reopened/edited` PR-body job (`pr:check-closing-keywords`). Live `GET repos/deftai/directive/rules/branches/master` returns one required status check: `Greptile Review`. Emitting a job name does not enroll it as merge-blocking.

**Failure mode:** AC1 stays false until a ruleset recut adds the new context. Adding a non-aggregator required check recuts #3168. A standalone `pull_request` workflow also runs on leftover-complete diffs that skip merge-gate.

**Disposition:** Put any remaining body or gate work on the existing merge-gate step and/or branch-gate job. Do not add `pre-pr-gate / checklist` as a required context.

## F4 — Checklist skip token makes untrusted PR body merge authority

`blocks-the-design`

**Evidence:** Injection/swarm lens fires (merge authority + untrusted PR body). Landed docs-impact (`packages/core/src/docs/docs-impact.ts`) parses closed `change_class` / `surfaces`; rationale is quoted, length-bounded, and "never a gate input" (template comment, module header, parse error). Closing-keywords is the second constrained PR-body parser. Tier 1 adds a third parser whose skip rule is an unconstrained `N/A -- <reason>` suffix. The first checklist item already embeds English "or N/A for <3 file changes" that is not that suffix.

**Failure mode:** An agent ticks every box, appends `N/A -- skipped`, or pastes `- [x]` lines into a custom body; merge is green with no RWLDL Read/Diff. Alternate checkbox spellings (`- [X]`, `* [x]`, Unicode) desynchronize GitHub's rendered boxes from the parser. Prompt-adjacent systems that echo PR bodies inherit skip prose as instruction-shaped text.

**Disposition:** Do not add a checkbox parser as merge authority. If a new body field is required, extend the docs-impact closed grammar as data, never as a skip predicate.

## F5 — Tiers 1-3 do not replace advisory RWLDL

`blocks-the-design`

**Evidence:** At this SHA the skill's automatable slices are iteration-lane lint plus one merge-chokepoint `deft check` / `task check`. Phase 1 Read (full-file review vs xBRIEF AC) and Phase 4 Diff (scope creep, gate-integrity) stay human-judgement; the issue keeps those phases. CI already runs `task check:merge` on non-artifact-only PRs. Stop 1 already carves the local-check-skip slice of PR #632 as covered by that job.

**Failure mode:** Binding Tiers 1-3 records a green checklist plus a SHA JSON as "pre-PR ran." Agents skip Read/Diff under the same speed pressure as PR #632. The slices that needed the skill stay advisory while the lean claims replacement.

**Disposition:** Leave human RWLDL phases advisory. Close the automatable slice by pointing at existing merge-gate plus docs-impact. Strike the target's "sufficient replacement" conjunct from the lean.

## F6 — T4 required-check language waits on #634

`sharpens-framing`

**Evidence:** Umbrella #635 current-shape comment 5221143936 (pass-1): "Tier commitments for **#604** / **#633** still wait on ladder discussion." #634 remains GitHub-open and "needs discussion before scoping." Thread comment 4307232478 parks #634 as non-blocking for #633 delivery; the umbrella shape still holds the tier-commitment wait.

**Failure mode:** A child that mints a new required-check T4 example writes the ladder before #634 exists.

**Disposition:** Keep #633 bindable as retarget-to-existing-gates. Leave new required-check / T4 floor language on #634.

## F7 — Filed implementation shape fights current `pr:*` rails

`sharpens-framing`

**Evidence:** `tasks/pr.yml` already dispatches TS `engine:invoke` verbs (`check-closing-keywords`, `watch`, `merge-ready`, …). `check:framework-source` is "TS-only after #1860". `tests/content` at this SHA contains `snapshots` only; pre-PR content locks live in `packages/core/src/content-contracts/skills/`. The skill forbids a fourth probe of the merge chokepoint. AC5 asks a `tests/content/` existence test of a new Action file.

**Failure mode:** `scripts/pre_pr_check.py` plus a Python content test reopens the python-free / #1860 port path and adds a second name for `task check`.

**Disposition:** If a `pr:ready` verb is wanted later, make it a TS engine alias of the existing chokepoint, with no marker file and no extra CI context.

## Footnotes

- `footnote` Stop 1 grep / workflow / template / skill anchors re-verified at the dispatch SHA; they hold.
- `footnote` Parent epic #635 and #634 remain GitHub-open (REST `issues/635`, `issues/634`).
- `footnote` RC3 lesson 5 in `meta/lessons.md` is writer/detector banner symmetry (#572). AC5 "Action file exists" does not instantiate that contract. A marker JSON would, and F1 shows AC7 left that contract unset.
- `footnote` Consumer-side Action rollout is already out of scope on the body.

## Injection / swarm lens

The target changes merge authority and consumes untrusted PR-body input, so the lens applies. F1 and F4 are the hits: gitignored `.deft/` is occupancy/scratch in swarm worktrees; promoting a file there to merge proof shares state workers already write. Checkbox / `N/A` prose in the PR body is agent-controlled. Existing controls are the docs-impact closed grammar (rationale never a gate input) and closing-keywords.

## Road not taken

Fork 1 (land Tiers 1-3 as filed) is the recorded target; it fails F1-F5. Fork 3 (drop checklist CI, keep only a `pr:ready` marker) still fails F1. Flip condition for reviving Tiers 2-3: a canonical marker spec whose writer CI itself runs, bit-identical detector, no gitignore hole, and no extra required-check name — which collapses to `task check:merge` plus `verify:docs-impact`.

## Verdict

The refutation succeeds. P1 is real, but Tiers 1–3 are neither executable nor sufficient as filed. The checklist rule conflicts with the current template, the local marker has no trust-preserving route into CI, and a workflow check does not become merge-required merely by existing. The authority boundary for untrusted PR-body input is also unspecified.

## Re-verified inventory

- At dispatch SHA `7712f482781c4885fd9d395756e2c316785730dd`, `git grep` returns zero hits for `pr:ready`, `pre-pr-complete`, or `pre-pr-gate`; `.github/workflows/` has no pre-PR gate.
- CI already runs `task check:merge` and `task verify:docs-impact` in both primary and failover merge-gate lanes. The latter is existing prior art for fetching a PR body through REST, parsing closed fields as data, and comparing them with the diff ([CI lines 181–197](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/7712f482781c4885fd9d395756e2c316785730dd/.github/workflows/ci.yml#L181-L197), [REST/parser transport](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/7712f482781c4885fd9d395756e2c316785730dd/packages/core/src/docs/docs-impact.ts#L518-L535)).
- The pre-PR skill separates the semantic Read/Write/Diff loop from the one full merge chokepoint and explicitly says not to add another full-gate probe ([lines 63–72](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/7712f482781c4885fd9d395756e2c316785730dd/content/skills/deft-directive-pre-pr/SKILL.md#L63-L72)).
- Live REST measurement during this review found no classic branch-protection object and one effective `master` required status check: `Greptile Review`. No Actions check from this repository is currently required.

## F1 — blocks-the-design — The literal checklist rule rejects an honest pre-merge PR

**Evidence.** The pinned template has three unchecked boxes under `## Checklist` and two more under `## Post-Merge` ([lines 24–32](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/7712f482781c4885fd9d395756e2c316785730dd/.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md#L24-L32)). A section-aware count reproduced `pre_merge_unchecked=3` and `post_merge_unchecked=2`. The proposed rule says any unchecked box without an `N/A -- reason` suffix fails, while the structural template recut is explicitly deferred. The current pre-merge checklist also contains no RWLDL item.

**Concrete failure mode.** Applied literally, every honest PR is red because issue auto-close verification and the one-time branch-protection action cannot occur before merge. Authors must falsely check future work, mark it N/A, delete the section, or exploit whatever undocumented section heuristic the parser happens to use. Even a parser scoped to the current `## Checklist` can be satisfied without running RWLDL because none of its three items attest that loop.

**Disposition consequence.** Tier 1 cannot bind as written. The same change must define a closed, pre-merge-only schema, explicitly exclude post-merge tasks, and decide whether it verifies declarations or outcomes. Deferring the needed template shape while shipping its parser reverses writer/detector symmetry.

## F2 — blocks-the-design — The head-SHA marker has no satisfiable provenance path

**Evidence.** The proposal makes `.deft/pre-pr-complete.<head-sha>.json` local and ignored, then asks CI to verify it through either a workflow artifact or a tracked hash manifest. At the pinned SHA, `.gitignore` already ignores `.deft/*`, so a PR checkout cannot contain that local file. GitHub's artifact API supports listing, downloading, and deleting workflow artifacts—not creating an artifact from an arbitrary local process; artifacts are produced in workflow runs and shared between their jobs ([GitHub artifact API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/artifacts)).

**Concrete failure mode.** The alternatives form a trilemma:

1. An ignored local marker is invisible to the GitHub runner.
2. A CI-produced artifact proves only that CI ran; it does not prove the author or agent completed semantic Read/Write/Diff, and CI already runs the mechanical merge chokepoint.
3. A tracked manifest containing its own commit's head SHA is self-invalidating: committing the manifest changes that SHA. If it instead records an earlier SHA or a freely authored digest, it is stale or forgeable.

The JSON fields (`timestamp`, `iteration count`, AC summary) remain author assertions unless a trusted principal signs or independently measures them.

**Disposition consequence.** Tier 3 must be dropped or replaced with a trusted attestation outside the commit graph, such as a dedicated GitHub App check-run bound to the exact head SHA and expected source. If the actual goal is deterministic product quality rather than proof that a human/agent followed prose, run the automatable outcomes directly in CI and stop claiming the marker proves the semantic loop.

## F3 — blocks-the-design — The PR cannot make its new check merge-required

**Evidence.** `gh api repos/deftai/directive/rules/branches/master` returned only `required_status_checks=[Greptile Review]`; `branches/master/protection` returned 404 because enforcement is via an organization ruleset. The pinned CI map's own historical claim says only its TypeScript aggregator was required and the merge-gate was not ([lines 43–65](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/7712f482781c4885fd9d395756e2c316785730dd/.github/workflows/ci.yml#L43-L65)), so tree prose is already stale relative to live authority. GitHub requires branch protection or a ruleset to name required checks; producing a check run does not make it required ([protected-branch semantics](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-protected-branches/about-protected-branches)).

**Concrete failure mode.** The new job can fail while merge remains allowed. Conversely, if a check is later required but the workflow does not report on every relevant path, it can strand PRs in pending. The filed trigger omits `reopened` and, if the documented merge-queue rollout occurs, `merge_group`; GitHub explicitly requires the latter for required Actions checks used by a merge queue ([required-check troubleshooting](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/how-tos/merge-and-close-pull-requests/troubleshooting-required-status-checks)). The requested context spelling `pre-pr-gate / checklist` is also not established by merely naming a workflow and a job; rulesets match the exact reported check name.

**Disposition consequence.** “Required” needs an explicit deployment surface outside this repository PR: exact check name/source, organization-ruleset change, bypass policy, always-reporting triggers, and a post-change REST assertion. Without that, AC1 and the T4 claim are false. This can be recut as a repository change plus a named operator-owned ruleset step, or as an organization-required workflow/App whose policy is independently managed.

## F4 — blocks-the-design — The merge gate is controlled by the input it is meant to judge

**Evidence.** GitHub documents `github.event.pull_request.body` as attacker-controlled input and warns against allowing it to flow into executable contexts ([script-injection guidance](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/security/script-injections)). It also documents that `pull_request` runs the workflow from the PR merge commit, while `pull_request_target` uses the trusted base context and therefore requires strict hardening ([event trust boundary](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/securely-using-pull_request_target)). The filed design specifies a new `pull_request` Action but no trusted-code source, permissions, input transport, or same-PR gate-change policy.

**Concrete failure mode.** A PR can alter the workflow/parser that emits the supposedly authoritative context, or a naïve implementation can interpolate crafted body text into `run:` and execute it. Switching casually to `pull_request_target` makes this worse if head code is checked out or secrets/write permissions remain available. The marker is a second untrusted shared-state input with no identity or signature.

**Disposition consequence.** The design needs a base-controlled checker before it can carry merge authority: for example, a hardened `pull_request_target` metadata-only workflow with read-only permissions and no head checkout, an organization-required workflow, or an external App. Read the body from the event file or REST and parse it as bounded data; never interpolate it into shell. Bind the required context to the expected App/source where available.

## F5 — sharpens-framing — The implementation sketch is stale and duplicates the current chokepoint

**Evidence.** The dispatch tree contains zero `.py` files. Current architecture says the Python runtime and `scripts/*.py` were removed and explicitly says not to add work there ([architecture line 27](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/7712f482781c4885fd9d395756e2c316785730dd/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md#L27)); the issue still proposes `scripts/pre_pr_check.py`. The pre-PR skill already defines one full `deft check` merge chokepoint, and CI already invokes `task check:merge`. Separately, the parent epic's [current-shape record](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/635#issuecomment-5221143936) says #634 still blocks tier commitments for #633, while #634 uses `T0`–`T6`; this issue independently calls its three components “Tiers 1–3.”

**Concrete failure mode.** Implementing the sketch reintroduces a retired runtime, creates a second orchestration path that can drift from `check:merge`, and overloads “tier” with two incompatible meanings.

**Disposition consequence.** Keep any local convenience command as a thin TypeScript/Taskfile route to existing checks, not a new Python checker or second full gate. Call the three components layers/stages, and reserve determinism-tier claims for the #634 decision.

## F6 — footnote — The incident proves the pain, not this remedy

REST re-check of [PR #632](https://github.com/deftai/directive/pull/632) confirms that its custom body had no template checkboxes and its recorded check-runs were green. That strongly supports P1. It does not supply provenance for a local marker or make an unconfigured status check required, so it adds no disposition weight for the filed mechanism.

## Road not taken and flip condition

The strongest case for the proposal is the composition: a visible declaration catches omitted template content, a head-bound result invalidates on later commits, and CI turns omission into a red signal. I would accept that shape if it had (1) a pre-merge-only closed declaration, (2) a non-self-referential trusted attestation channel, (3) base-controlled parsing of untrusted text, and (4) a measured ruleset rollout that makes the exact check required.

The smaller and stronger recut is to enforce objectively reproducible outcomes at the existing CI boundary: reuse the closed-field/REST pattern from `verify:docs-impact`, run the mechanical checks against the tested SHA through the existing merge chokepoint, and treat semantic Read/Write/Diff as review practice rather than pretending a user-authored marker proves it. If proof of local execution is truly the product requirement, that is a separate identity-and-attestation design, not a JSON file in or beside the commit.

### F1 — "Physically block a PR from merging" is a settings property this PR cannot set, and admins are exempt today — `blocks-the-design`

Evidence (live, read at dispatch):

- `repos/deftai/directive/branches/master` → `required_status_checks.contexts = ["TypeScript (build + lint + test)"]`, `enforcement_level: non_admins`.

### Injection / swarm lens

Fires: this target moves merge authority onto untrusted, author-controlled PR-body text.

1. **Script-injection sink.** The safe in-tree pattern is `ci.yml`'s: pass `GITHUB_PR_NUMBER` via `env` and fetch the body over REST inside a TS program. A composite or `run:` Action that interpolates `${{ github.event.pull_request.body }}` into a shell step executes attacker-authored text on the runner. Tier 1 must state the non-interpolating shape as an acceptance criterion, not leave it to implementation.
2. **Free text as authority.** `N/A -- <reason>` inverts the recorded docs-impact rule that body rationale is data and never a gate input. The deterministic control is a closed enum cross-checked against a diff detector (F7) — not prose presence, and not reviewer attention.
3. **Forks.** A fork cannot produce a workflow-scoped artifact, and a committed manifest is forgeable by the contributor. Tier 3 therefore either blocks all external PRs or is worthless on them. Name which.
4. **Trigger.** Keep `pull_request`. `pull_request_target` plus body parsing plus a write token would hand a fork author a privileged surface.

### Road not taken

I considered accepting Tier 1 alone as a cheap ratchet and deferring Tiers 2-3. Rejected: with F1 unfixed the check is advisory by a different mechanism, and with F7 unfixed it stays advisory even after it is made required. A ratchet that ratchets nothing costs a required-check slot and a maintenance surface.

### Steelman, and what would flip me

Strongest case for landing as filed: the gap is real and re-verified; attestation surfaces do change behaviour even when forgeable; and the topology argument (F1) has been open since #57, so "fix topology first" risks shipping nothing. Two facts would flip my verdict: (a) a live `required_status_checks` entry naming the new context with `enforce_admins: true`, and (b) a marker whose validity CI computes from the diff alone, with no self-written token. With both, the tier stack is sufficient. With neither, it is a badge.

### Recommended fork

Fork 2 (retarget to existing surfaces), sequenced:

1. Settings: repo-scoped ruleset adding the `Merge gate (task check)` aggregator as required, with admin enforcement. Validate the #3678 artifact-only skip path against required-check semantics before flipping.
2. One `verify:changelog-unreleased` on `check:framework-source` — the only checklist item with no detector.
3. Shrink the template checklist to items that have detectors; move `## Post-Merge` out of `- [ ]` syntax so no parser can be pointed at it.
4. Drop Tier 2 and Tier 3, or refile the marker separately as a diff-digest artifact with the #4383 first-mint binding problem named up front.

metadata.issueBody:
## Summary

Make the `skills/deft-directive-pre-pr` (RWLDL) quality gate deterministic by moving enforcement from doc-only `!` rules in `AGENTS.md` to CI-level checks that physically block a PR from merging until the gate has run. `lessons.md` is not a reliable backstop: not indexed, not chained from any skill, and not consulted mandatorily.

## Why now

PR #632 (merged 2026-04-23) silently skipped three `AGENTS.md` `!` gates:

- `skills/deft-directive-pre-pr/SKILL.md` (RWLDL loop) -- not run
- Local `task check` pre-commit gate -- not run (only post-push CI green was confirmed)
- `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` checklist -- not filled (a custom PR body replaced it; zero `- [ ]` boxes appeared)

Root cause: the gates are advisory. None have a CI-side enforcement, so compliance relies entirely on agent discipline. Under speed pressure (post-release, mid-Blacksmith-incident), that discipline silently degraded. Post-merge audit caught it, but only by accident.

This is exactly the failure mode `meta/lessons.md` section `## RC3 Validation on Windows (2026-04)` lesson 5 warns about: rules with only docs-level enforcement must be paired with a regression test asserting writer/detector symmetry. The pre-PR gate is doc-only today.

## Proposed deliverable (Tiers 1-3 in one PR)

### Tier 1 -- CI PR-body checklist enforcement

New GitHub Action (on `pull_request` opened/edited/synchronize) that:

- Parses the PR body for `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` checklist markers
- Fails the check if any `- [ ]` box is unchecked without an `N/A -- <reason>` suffix
- Emits a required status check `pre-pr-gate / checklist`

Catches the PR #632 failure mode (custom body + no checklist) at PR-open time, not post-merge audit.

### Tier 2 -- `task pr:ready` + marker artifact

- New `scripts/pre_pr_check.py` that runs the mechanically automatable slices of RWLDL: file-list-from-diff Read phase, `task check` Lint phase, `git diff master` Diff phase
- On clean exit, writes `.deft/pre-pr-complete.<head-sha>.json` (diff hash, timestamp, iteration count, vBRIEF acceptance-criteria coverage summary)
- New `task pr:ready` Taskfile entry wrapping the script
- Documented in `skills/deft-directive-pre-pr/SKILL.md` as the canonical invocation; existing RWLDL phase content stays as the human-judgement slice

### Tier 3 -- CI marker cross-check

Extend the Tier 1 Action to also verify that a `.deft/pre-pr-complete.<head-sha>.json` marker is present for the PR head SHA. If absent, the CI check fails with an actionable message pointing at `task pr:ready`. Closes the loophole where an agent checks the boxes without actually running the loop.

## Out of scope (follow-ups)

- **Tier 4**: Structural PR-template change with machine-checkable items (`- [ ] RWLDL iterations: N`, `- [ ] task check exit 0 at <timestamp>`, etc.) -- file separately once Tiers 1-3 land.
- Git pre-push hook -- portability issues (hooks do not clone); defer unless Tiers 1-3 prove insufficient.
- Consumer-side rollout: deft ships the same template + Action to consumer projects via `deft-directive-setup`; track separately.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Opening a PR with an empty or unchecked `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` checklist produces a failing CI status check that blocks merge on the configured protected branches.
2. `task pr:ready` exits 0 on a clean branch and writes `.deft/pre-pr-complete.<head-sha>.json`; exits non-zero with an actionable message when `task check` fails, the diff is dirty against the base, or the loop did not converge.
3. Opening a PR without a marker file matching the head SHA produces a failing CI status check.
4. `skills/deft-directive-pre-pr/SKILL.md` names `task pr:ready` as the canonical RWLDL entrypoint without removing the human-judgement phases (Read semantic review, Diff scope-creep check).
5. A regression test in `tests/content/` asserts the GH Action file exists and references both the checklist parser and the marker check (writer/detector symmetry rule from RC3 lesson 5).
6. `meta/lessons.md` gains an entry documenting the PR #632 root cause and the deterministic replacement.
7. `.gitignore` excludes `.deft/pre-pr-complete.*.json` so marker files never get committed; Action reads them from a workflow-scoped artifact upload instead, or from a git-tracked hash-only manifest -- decide in design.

## References

- Triggering session: PR #632 (merged 2026-04-23) -- post-merge audit exposed the skipped gates
- Pattern prior art: `tests/content/test_taskfile_cli_args.py`, `test_taskfile_paths.py`, `test_machine_generated_banner.py`, `test_skill_frontmatter.py` -- all examples of turning doc-only deft conventions into CI-enforced content tests
- Governing rule: `meta/lessons.md` section RC3 lesson 5 (writer/detector symmetry mandate)
- Skill under enforcement: `skills/deft-directive-pre-pr/SKILL.md`
- Template under enforcement: `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`

---

## Linked issues

Part of **#635** (umbrella: skill-system maturity + framework-rule determinism).

- **#75** — skill auto-discovery (infrastructure: authoritative skill inventory)
- **#604** — resolver eval + check-resolvable audit (routing quality gate)
- **#607** — failure-to-skill protocol (policy: recurrable failures become skills, not prose lessons)
- **#633** — pre-PR quality gate deterministic (concrete T4 worked example)
- **#634** — determinism-tier ladder governance (meta-rule generalising the pattern)
